outcome: uterine tachysystole with fetal cardiotocography abnormalities
duration of labor from IOL to delivery
cohort: The study included 100 women with fetal growth restriction requiring induction of labor.
finding: Vaginal misoprostol at 25 mg was found to be more effective than a Foley catheter for induction of labor in pregnancies affected by fetal growth restriction, with few women experiencing uterine tachysystole with cardiotocography abnormalities in either group.
mod_finding: More women in the misoprostol group achieved vaginal delivery within 12 hours and were less likely to deliver by lower-segment cesarean delivery compared to the Foley catheter group.
